newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs steady to firm, W. Africa also stron.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs steady to firm, W. Africa also stron.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates were steady to firm on Thursday, with most other sectors also firm, brokers said.

One broker pointed to the large number of Middle East VLCC fixtures over the last couple of days -- nine each on Wednesday and Tuesday -- as well as a lack of tonnage. "It's still moving up...It could improve even more next week," he added.
He put Mideast/Japan voyages at W67.5/70, Mideast/Singapore at W60 and Mideast/West at W55/57.5.
The West Africa market also remained firm, with 130 tonne (million barrel) cargoes to the U.S. Gulf at W107.5.
To the Atlantic coast they were at W110. A U.S. broker attributed the strength in this sector to good interest rather than a shortage of vessels.
Current West Africa million barrel rates are some 17 points above the February average of W90.65, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.
The inter-U.K./Cont market also maintained its recent firmness, with 80,000 tonne cargoes fixed at W135/140.
"Activity is a bit lower at the moment but if you look at tonnage, there is not that much around, so I think the market will stay firm over the next few days," another broker said.
The Mediterranean market was quiet, with brokers saying it was hard to predict how rates will move from the current W102.5 for 130,000 tonne cargoes and W107.5 for 80,000 tonnes.
The North Sea-U.S. sector was also quiet, with VLCCs assessed around W65/70 and 130,000 tonners at W95.
Inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W195 on growing enquiry, especially from the Baltic, while cross-Med was steady at about W220, brokers said.
The Caribs/upcoast market remained strong, with both 70,000 tonne crude and 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes at W200.
